title: Platform systems & services playbook, runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap - 2025 Q3
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Summary:

This document is the canonical platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference (eng-platform). It consolidates systems & services inventory, standard runbooks, dashboard and alerting recommendations, common how-tos, the near-term roadmap, and a short retrospective on major incidents and operational learnings from the last 12 months. Intended audience: on-call engineers, SREs, platform owners, and product partners.

Scope:
- Production services that serve inference traffic (api-gateway, inference-router, runtime-pool, kv-cache, batching-service).
- Observability: Grafana dashboards, Prometheus metrics, Datadog traces, and SLO/alerting rules.
- Runbooks for P0–P2 incidents and standard maintenance procedures.
- Roadmap items through Q1 2026.

Owner and Contacts:
- Platform team lead / doc owner: Priya Natarajan (priya@redwood.example.com)
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.example.com (primary paged via PagerDuty)
- Escalation: Level 1 -> oncall; Level 2 -> Platform Reliability (Liam O'Connor); Level 3 -> Engineering Manager (Jia Chen)

Systems and Services Inventory (high level):
| Service name | Primary responsibility | Owners | SLO (p99 latency) | Notes |
| api-gateway | edge routing and auth | eng-platform | 200ms | TLS termination, WAF rules |
| inference-router | model routing, fallbacks | eng-serving-runtime | 50ms | Smart routing, model variants |
| runtime-pool | GPU-backed inference runtime | eng-serving-runtime | 95% requests served within target | Handles batching & quantized kernels |
| kv-cache | prefix/KV caching for tokens | eng-serving-runtime | hit rate >= 60% | Redis-cluster w/ cross-region replication |
| batching-service | request batching orchestration | eng-platform | batch latency <= 10ms | Autoscaling hooks |

Dashboards and Observability Standards:
- Dashboard ownership: every service must have a named dashboard owned by the service's oncall. Dashboards must surface SLOs, error budgets, top-5 traces, and capacity metrics.
- Required dashboards (template names):
  - "Service Overview" — high-level traffic, errors, latency percentiles, SLO meter
  - "Capacity & Utilization" — CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, batch sizes
  - "Error Analysis" — 5xx breakdown, model-failure rates, top error traces
  - "Cost & Throughput" — token/sec, GPU-hours, cache hit ratio

Grafana panels and Prometheus metrics (recommended):
- Requests: inference_requests_total, inference_requests_errors_total
- Latency: inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket (p50/p90/p99)
- Batching: batch_size_histogram, batch_wait_seconds
- Cache: kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_requests_total
- Capacity: gpu_utilization_percent, gpu_memory_free_bytes

Alerting baseline (alert severity and example rules):
1) P0 — System-wide outage or loss of all inference capacity
   - Trigger: service_down_count > 2 across regions OR p99_latency > 2s and error_rate > 5% for > 2 minutes
   - PagerDuty: SEV-0 -> page oncall + manager escalation
   - Runbook: see P0 runbook below

2) P1 — Degraded performance impacting customers
   - Trigger: p99_latency > SLO * 2 for > 5 minutes OR error_rate > 2%
   - PagerDuty: SEV-1 -> page oncall
   - Actions: scale runtime-pool, activate failover routing, open incident channel

3) P2 — Operational issues that may cause future impact
   - Trigger: kv_cache_hit_rate < 40% for 10m, batch queue growing > 2k
   - Notification: slack alert to #platform-ops, no immediate page

Alert tuning notes:
- Use suppression windows for expected maintenance (e.g., scheduled kernel upgrades).
- Add dynamic thresholds tied to baseline traffic percentiles to avoid alert storms during traffic spikes.
- Annotate significant alerts with runbook links and 'last tuned' metadata.

Runbooks (extracts):
1) P0 — Full inference outage
- Summary: Top-level failure where > 50% of inference requests fail or p99 latency exceeds 2s globally.
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and create incident channel (#inc-platform-sev0-<timestamp>).
  2. Check provider status pages (GCP/AWS/Azure) for region-level problems.
  3. Verify api-gateway health: curl health endpoint and check Grafana "Service Overview".
  4. If api-gateway healthy, check inference-router for saturated routes: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` and `kubectl top pods -n inference`.
  5. Check runtime-pool GPU utilization and queue depths. If GPUs saturated, trigger emergency scale (see Emergency scale section below).
  6. If responsible for model runtime failure, fallback routing: switch routing policy to "fallback-model-variant" via admin UI or CLI `rdwctl routing set --policy fallback-model-variant`.
  7. Document actions in the incident channel, add timeline entries, and assign owners for each remediation step.
- Emergency scale (quick):
  - For dedicated clouds: increase nodegroup desired count via autoscaling group or terraform runbooks (console-approved escalation).
  - For hosted: notify infra to provision burst capacity and update routing weights to route to dedicated pools.

2) P1 — Degraded latency / increased p50-p99
- Triage:
  1. Identify impacted service (use top traces).
  2. Check batching-service: are batches too small? `curl /metrics | grep batch_size` and look for median batch size < expected.
  3. If batch sizes dropped, check request fanout patterns from api-gateway. Consider enabling adaptive batching (feature flag: platform.adaptive_batching=true).
  4. If backend CPU/GPU saturation, scale runtime-pool or throttle lower-priority routes.

Maintenance & Standard Procedures (How-tos):
- Deploying a dashboard template:
  1. Clone the canonical dashboard (dashboards/team-templates/platform-service.json).
  2. Update variables: service name, owners, prometheus datasource.
  3. Test panels in staging, then import to production grafana with tag `owned-by:<team>`.
- Safely applying a runtime kernel upgrade:
  1. Schedule a 2-hour maintenance window during low traffic.
  2. Run canary rollout to 2 nodes, run perf suite (link: /ci/benchmarks/runtime-kernel-smoke).
  3. Monitor SLOs for 30 minutes, then progressively roll to remainder, abort on > 10% regression in p99 or error spike.

Roadmap (near term, prioritized):
- Q4 2025:
  - (P0) Unified dashboard templates for all inference services (owner-onboarding automation) — ETA: 2025-10-15
  - (P1) Adaptive batching improvement (reduce tail latency for small requests) — ETA: 2025-11-30
  - (P1) Cache sharding & eviction tuning to raise hit rate to 70% — ETA: 2025-12-15
- Q1 2026:
  - (P0) Cross-region automated failover with traffic-weighted routing and model variant compatibility checks — ETA: 2026-02-28
  - (P2) Cost metering per-token by model variant for chargeback and optimizations — ETA: 2026-03-31

Retrospective (major operational lessons):
- Incident: 2025-05-03 model rollout caused p99 spike in inference-router for 3 hours. Root cause: a miscompiled attention kernel in a new runtime image.
  - What went well: canary testing caught the issue on staging earlier but rollout automation skipped policy gates.
  - Action items: add mandatory pre-rollout SLO gate in CI, require binary signatures for runtime images, and add immediate rollback toggle per cluster.
- Incident: 2025-02-17 Redis cluster failover caused temporary kv_cache hit-rate collapse.
  - What went well: automated failover succeeded but cache warm-up was slow.
  - Action items: implement staged cache warm-up (prefetch for hot prefixes) and increase replication factor in critical regions.

Onboarding checklist for new platform engineers:
1. Access: request membership to `eng-platform` and `platform-ops` PagerDuty/Slack channels.
2. Read this playbook and confirm knowledge of P0/P1 runbooks.
3. Pair with oncall for two rotations.
4. Complete dashboard ownership handoff for one service.

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- rdwctl (CLI): `rdwctl service status inference-router --region us-west1`
- Kubernetes: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide`
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/PLATFORM/Platform-Service-Overview
- Incident template: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/template

Change log:
- 2025-08-20 - created by Priya Natarajan
- 2025-10-12 - added adaptive batching notes (reviewed by Jia Chen)
- 2026-02-10 - updated roadmap and retrospective entries after Q1 planning

For questions or proposed updates, please open a PR against this page and add reviewers from the `eng-platform` team.
